title: fix(spec): stop the ETL-retirement entry promising an executed connector sync
body:
Fixes #17159

Clause-②: no — this PR puts no new key on any published payload and moves no accept set. It corrects one published SENTENCE in a D3 semantic entry and the three generated projections of it. Declared by the `domain:spec` execution seat (session `session_01MkQhmuuJAVDjmeWNixwDDH`), which is the declarer for this pair; the card's governing claim comment carries the same value.

## What

The D3 semantic entry `etl-pipeline-layer-retired` told an author displaced by the ETL
layer's retirement that connector-attached synchronisation is `ConnectorSchema.syncConfig`,
"which **IS parsed and executed**". Parsed is true. Executed never was.

`replacement` is an ADR-0087 D4 **projected** field, so the sentence is published, not
internal: it ships verbatim in `packages/spec/spec-changes.json` (twice — the flat entry at
`:739` and the composed record at `:1818`), which is in this package's `files[]`, and it
renders into `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md:443`.

## The measurement — re-derived on this branch, every zero with a lit control

**Nothing reads `syncConfig`.**

| probe | reading |
|:--|:--|
| `git grep -n -P '\bsyncConfig\b' -- packages ':!packages/spec/**'` | 2 hits, both **comment lines** in `packages/qa/dogfood/test/expression-conformance.ledger.ts:340,342` — prose about the key, not a reader |
| lit control, same grep machinery | `ConnectorSchema` outside `packages/spec` → **16 files** (4 connector packages, `service-automation/src/engine.ts`, qa). The exclusion is not eating the corpus |
| the parse site | `AutomationEngine.registerConnector` and `registerDegradedConnector` (`packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts:3333,3412`) run `ConnectorSchema.parse(def)` and store the parsed definition in `this.connectors`. Read back off it: `parsed.actions` only (`:3334`, `:3475`). `syncConfig` — never |
| already stated at the schema | `packages/spec/src/integration/connector.zod.ts:257` — "`syncConfig` has no reader outside `packages/spec`, no engine schedules…" — landed with the `syncConfig.schedule` retirement under ADR-0049 |

**Sibling repos.** `objectui` was read at the `.objectui-sha` **pin** this repo builds against,
`53ded82bf7a494f54e344e19099dbf00854b8694`, via `git show`, not at that checkout's HEAD
(`3fbdd4a2…`, an unrelated branch). It has `syncConfig` hits — and they are the
**near-synonym trap**, so they are read rather than counted: `packages/react/src/hooks/useOffline.ts:263`
is `sync: syncConfig`, a destructuring rename of the `OfflineConfig.sync` option on an
offline-queue React hook. That file imports nothing from `@objectstack/spec` (its only import
is `react`). Zero relation to `ConnectorSchema.syncConfig`. Lit controls at the same pin:
`@objectstack/spec` → many files, `connector` → many files, so the pinned tree is readable.
`objectstack-ai/cloud` could **not** be read from this session (`add_repo` → no access); that
half of the sweep is declared unmeasured, not green.

## The sentence

**Before** — "connector-attached synchronisation is `ConnectorSchema.syncConfig`
(`integration/connector.zod.ts`), which IS parsed and executed"

**After** — "connector-attached synchronisation is `ConnectorSchema.syncConfig`
(`integration/connector.zod.ts`), which is PARSED AND VALIDATED but NOT EXECUTED — a declared
shape, not a running sync. `AutomationEngine.registerConnector` runs `ConnectorSchema.parse`
and stores the parsed definition; nothing reads `syncConfig` back off it, and the key has no
reader outside `packages/spec` at all — the same measurement that retired
`syncConfig.schedule` in 18 under ADR-0049 (#16320). What the platform DOES execute on a
connector is its `actions`: a flow's `connector_action` node resolves the registered handler
and awaits it, so an author who needs data actually moved drives it from there."

A false promise is not replaced with a vague one: the reader is told what the block **is**,
what **happens** to it, and where the executed surface actually lives. That last clause is
measured too — `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/connector-nodes.ts:61,107`
resolves the handler and awaits it.

The retirement itself is untouched. No key moves, no accept set moves, no schema changes.

## The projections are generated, never hand-edited

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:migration-registry` → `gen:spec-changes` → `gen:upgrade-guide`,
each exit 0, then `check:generated` — **all 15 generated artifacts up to date**, including
`check:migration-registry`, `check:spec-changes` and `check:upgrade-guide`.

Absence, with its exit code captured before any pipe: `git grep -n 'IS parsed and executed'`
over the whole tree → **exit 1 (no match)**; the same grep for `no protocol surface replaces it`
→ exit 0, 5 sites. The one deliberate remaining occurrence of the old wording in this branch is
inside the changeset, which quotes it in order to correct it.

## Ablation — the pin is RED on the old sentence, GREEN on the new one

Run from the **committed** tree, restore leg pinned to `HEAD`, with a `trap … EXIT INT TERM`
and absolute paths throughout.

1. `HEAD` blob hashes recorded for both files first.
2. Mutation: the old clause put back **in the entry**, then `gen:migration-registry` to project
   it into `registry.ts` — which is what the pin actually reads.
3. **On-disk proof read FIRST**, on the text that moved: entry `IS parsed and executed` = 1,
   `PARSED AND VALIDATED` = 0; `registry.ts` after regeneration = 1 / 0.
4. **RED**: `3 failed | 126 passed`. The three that fell are the claim pins. The anti-vacuity
   case and the "retirement still stands" case stayed green — correct: they guard against the
   entry vanishing, not against the sentence.
5. Restore proven by hash, never by an exit code:
   `7365e43bdde696804845fb82f58ffb688a7a13ca == HEAD blob`, `b48f5d6c634623ce62428bc0c181e16adc89a539 == HEAD blob`,
   and `git diff HEAD --stat` empty.
6. **GREEN**: `129 passed (129)`.

No `dist` preflight applies: the pin imports `./registry.js`, a relative sibling inside its own
package, so nothing resolves through `@objectstack/spec`'s `exports` into `dist/`.

## Verification

| run | result |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` | lock VERDICT command-exit **0** — run FIRST, so no dist-dependent file skipped itself |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` (`--project local`) | **0** — `Test Files 472 passed (472)`, `Tests 13439 passed (13439)`, none skipped |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test:repo` (`--project repo`) | **0** — `Test Files 30 passed (30)`, `Tests 520 passed (520)`; re-run at the final commit because this diff is exactly the prose those cross-corpus scanners read |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` | see the table row re-stated in the round report |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` | **0** — 15/15 up to date |
| derived gate families, `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` | **84 derived, 84 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN** — reconciled with `--ran`, every line carrying `:: exit N` so the zero is derived rather than claimed |
| `pnpm exec eslint . --no-inline-config --format json` | **0** — the WHOLE repo, not a narrowed slice: **6656 files**, 0 errors, 0 warnings, at `d41a2834a6` |
| control-character sweep over the six changed files | exit 1 (clean); same regex on a planted `0x01` byte exits 0 |

Four derived families first exited **3 = NOT MEASURED** (`check:doc-formula-expressions`,
`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:type-check-debt`) because they
read built output. The workspace closure was built and all four re-run; the last one OOMs at its
own default heap on this shared box and was re-run at `--max-old-space-size=8192`, which is a
deliberate raise, stated here rather than buried: **exit 0**, 5 ledger entries re-measured, none
above its recorded number.

## Changeset

`patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, and it is **measured**, not inherited from the card. Built first,
both build passes finished, then `npm pack --dry-run --json`:

- positive control — `spec-changes.json` **ships** (`files[]` names it); `dist/` ships; the new
  sentence is present twice in the packed `spec-changes.json` and in `dist/index.js`,
  `dist/index.mjs`, `dist/browser/index.js`, `dist/browser/index.mjs`
- negative control — `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` does **not** ship;
  `migrations.test.ts` does **not** ship; a planted marker string is absent from `dist/`

Published text moves, so `skip-changeset` would be wrong.

## 验收备注

**noted, not filed — nothing cross-checks a projected ledger string against the tree it
describes.** The triage asked for this to be named whether or not it is fixed here. The gate
family around `replacement` pins ledger-to-**projection** synchrony (`check:spec-changes`,
`check:upgrade-guide`) and says nothing about ledger-to-**reality**; `grep` over the repo finds
`.replacement` read by exactly three per-entry pins plus the CLI and the guide generator — one
pin added per defect, after the fact. This PR adds the fourth. It is an observation about a
missing capability, not a reproducible defect, a declared-contract violation or an authoring
trap, so it is recorded here rather than opened as a card; the carrier is whoever adds the next
per-entry pin in `migrations.test.ts`, and the reasoning is written into that pin's docblock so
it is not re-derived from scratch.

**noted, not filed — the two neighbouring clauses in the same sentence were spot-checked and
both hold.** `shared/mapping.zod.ts`'s `transform` really is applied row by row on the REST
import path (`packages/rest/src/import-mapping.ts`, `applyMappingToRows`) and
`packages/spec/liveness/mapping.json` exists; `system/job.zod.ts` scheduling really is executed
(`packages/services/service-job/src/cron-job-adapter.ts` drives `croner`, and
`liveness/job.json` exists). No second false clause in this string.
